annotation.title_clean: Opening Statement of Chairman Jay Obernolte at Robots Made in America: Advancing U.S. Leadership in Manufacturing and Automation
annotation.title_en: Opening Statement of Chairman Jay Obernolte at Robots Made in America: Advancing U.S. Leadership in Manufacturing and Automation
annotation.authors_or_issuer: House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Chairman Jay Obernolte)
annotation.venue: House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology website
annotation.summary_en: Opening statement by House Science Committee subcommittee Chairman Obernolte at an April 2026 hearing on U.S. robotics leadership. He frames physical AI as a competitiveness issue versus China, promotes a national robotics strategy, and highlights his bipartisan National Commission on Robotics Act, NSF research funding, and NIST standards.
key_provisions_or_claims: Calls for a national robotics strategy to support manufacturing and workers
Introduced bipartisan National Commission on Robotics Act to evaluate U.S. competitiveness
Frames China's robotics investment as a competitive threat
Highlights NSF Foundational Research in Robotics program and NIST safety standards role
Envisions humanoid robots aiding factory work and elder care
